details.what_it_is: Step-by-step horticulture protocols and how-to guides.

topics.title: Homemade fertilizers: the mistakes that damage your plants
topics.key_message: It is not the ingredient itself that is the problem, but how you use it. The same material can feed your plant or burn it.

mistakes.mistake: Thick layer: forms an impermeable crust and attracts mushrooms/fungi
mistakes.right_method: Thin layer (< 5 mm / 0.2 in), mixed into the soil or diluted in water

mistakes.mistake: Fresh and whole: they ferment and can spread Fusarium
mistakes.right_method: Soak for 48 h, strain, use only the water

mistakes.mistake: Whole pieces: decompose too slowly (takes years to release anything)
mistakes.right_method: Grind into a fine powder; released usefully within one season

mistakes.mistake: Salted: causes osmotic burn of the roots
mistakes.right_method: Only if the food was cooked without salt

mistakes.mistake: Weekly application: tannins build up and cause chlorosis (yellowing)

mistakes.right_method: Use the same day, or refrigerate for up to 24 h

topics.summary: Homemade fertilizers work well as long as they are properly prepared and dosed: dilution, grinding, soaking, and moderate frequency.
